subsystems.name: Air contactor
subsystems.role: Captures carbon dioxide from ambient air at very low concentration.
parts: solid sorbent or amine-based capture material

subsystems.name: CO2 conversion reactor
subsystems.role: Turns captured CO2 into solid carbon in the form of carbon nanotubes.
parts: electrolysis cell with molten carbonate electrolyte

subsystems.name: Carbon nanotube processing
subsystems.role: Purifies, washes and functionalises the raw nanotube product for use in composites.

subsystems.name: Filament compounding
subsystems.role: Mixes carbon nanotubes uniformly into a polymer matrix to make a printable masterbatch.

subsystems.name: Filament extrusion
subsystems.role: Forms the composite into precise-diameter filament for 3D printers.

subsystems.name: Printing system
subsystems.role: Deposits the filament layer by layer into finished high-strength parts.

buildSteps.title: Capture CO2 from air
buildSteps.detail: Ambient air is drawn through a contactor where a sorbent binds carbon dioxide. The sorbent is then heated to release a concentrated CO2 stream.

buildSteps.title: Purify and pressurise the CO2
buildSteps.detail: Water vapour and contaminants are removed, and the gas is compressed or buffered for steady feed to the reactor.

buildSteps.title: Convert CO2 to carbon nanotubes
buildSteps.detail: In a molten carbonate electrolysis cell, CO2 is split at high temperature (around 750 °C) into solid carbon that grows as nanotubes on the cathode, releasing oxygen at the anode.

buildSteps.title: Wash and functionalise the nanotubes
buildSteps.detail: The cathode product is removed, washed to strip leftover salts, dried, and treated to improve bonding with polymers.

buildSteps.title: Compound with polymer
buildSteps.detail: Nanotubes are fed with polymer pellets into a twin-screw extruder, where they are dispersed to form a masterbatch with enhanced strength and conductivity.

buildSteps.title: Extrude printing filament
buildSteps.detail: The masterbatch is melted and drawn into filament of tightly controlled diameter (typically 1.75 mm), cooled and spooled.

buildSteps.title: Print the final part
buildSteps.detail: A fused-deposition 3D printer melts the filament and lays it down layer by layer, using a hardened nozzle to handle the abrasive nanotubes.

buildSteps.title: Test and post-process
buildSteps.detail: Parts are measured for mechanical strength, electrical conductivity and dimensional accuracy, and may be annealed to improve interlayer bonding.

prerequisites.why: Provides the CO2 feedstock without needing a concentrated industrial source.

prerequisites.tech: Electrochemical CO2 conversion to carbon nanotubes
prerequisites.why: Demonstrated in laboratories and small pilots using molten salt electrolysis, but not yet at industrial scale.
Commercial CNT-filled filaments exist, but none made from captured atmospheric CO2.
The printing hardware is mature; the challenge is adapting it to abrasive, high-loading nanotube composites.
DAC and high-temperature electrolysis are energy-intensive, so the climate benefit depends on clean power.

pathway.milestone: Separate demonstrations: DAC plants capture CO2, and lab reactors convert CO2 into carbon nanotubes.
pathway.unlocks: Proof that both halves of the process work independently.

pathway.milestone: Pilot coupling of a DAC unit to a CO2-to-nanotube reactor, producing kilogram-scale batches.
pathway.unlocks: Understanding of real-world integration, energy use and product consistency.

pathway.milestone: Commercial production of CO2-derived nanotube masterbatch and 3D printing filament.
pathway.unlocks: A market for carbon-negative materials that can compete on performance.

pathway.milestone: Distributed 'carbon printing' hubs that capture local CO2 and print large structural or functional parts on demand.
pathway.unlocks: A manufacturing route that permanently stores carbon in durable goods.
